newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to tell G7 forex stability important - source.
newsitem.headline: Japan to tell G7 forex stability important - source.

text.p: Japan will stress the importance of foreign exchange market stability when Group of Seven (G7) nations meet in Berlin this weekend, an international monetary source said on Wednesday.
The source, who did not want to be named, said that Japan also wanted to make clear that excessive yen volatility is unfavourable.

"For our part, we would like to make clear (at the G7 meeting) that forex stability holds significant importance and excessive appreciation or depreciation of the yen is unfavourable," the source told reporters.
The source said Japan's economy has been posting a recovery led by domestic demand that is firming.
The G7 nations are likely to spend a lot of time in exchanging opinions on macroeconomic factors in each country, he said.
Inflation in industrial countries, including G7 members, has subsided, while most G7 nations can expect steady growth this year, though the magnitude of growth may vary, he said.
Each country is also expected to describe its efforts towards fiscal reform and policies to reach that goal, he said.
At the G7 meeting, Japan will also explain its fiscal and financial reform plans which are part of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's comprehensive reform project, he said.
Finance ministers and central bank governors of the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- are to meet in Berlin on Saturday.

Asked how Japan would respond to a possible query from its G7 partners about the Japanese stock market's weakness, the source said: "We would say that we are closely monitoring the stock market movements and that the fundamental variables in Japan are good."
